**Lights can be shot out.** Lamps, light strips and computer screens break
when you shoot their glowing part. The whole fixture sputters for a moment and
goes dark, a screen's glass cracks over a black tube, and a moment later the
room loses the light that fixture gave it: the baked light fades from the
floors and walls around it, monsters and items there go dark, and the room's
own light level drops by the share that lamp provided. A room lit only by its
lamps ends up close to pitch black, with the flashlight as the only light left.
Bullets, shotgun pellets, imp and other fireballs, plasma, rockets, BFG balls
and exploding barrels all do it, and so do monsters' shots, so a gunfight wears
down the light of the room it happens in. A rocket or barrel breaks every lamp
within its blast radius that can see the explosion.

**Sparks.** Computer panels, tech walls and light fixtures throw short bursts of
blue sparks with a quick flash when they're hit, glowing or not. A breaking lamp
throws a bigger burst of white glass sparks.

**Kill shots carry on.** A bullet or pellet that kills what it hits keeps going
past the body, but only for sparks and lights: point-blank kills in front of a
wall of screens take some of them out too. The game itself still sees the shot
stop at the monster, so damage, demos and saves are unchanged.

All of this is render-only, like the window glass: monsters see and fight as
they always did, and the lights are back when you load a save or restart the
level. Both are on by default and can be turned off in **F4 → Combat → Shootable
lights** and **Kill shots carry on**. They need **Emissive textures**
on; the darkening needs **Baked static lights**.
